Brazil.text: The only team to play at every World Cup, and the only one to win it on four continents.
Brazil.evidence: It is the only national team to have played in all World Cup editions without missing an edition or needing to qualify through play-offs, and the only team to have won the World Cup in four different continents.

Germany.text: Gottfried Fuchs scored 10 goals in one game for Germany in 1912, a world record until 2001.
Germany.evidence: Gottfried Fuchs scored a world record 10 goals for Germany in a 16–0 win against Russia at the 1912 Olympics in Stockholm on 1 July, becoming the top scorer of the tournament; his international record was not surpassed until 2001

Argentina.text: No team has won more official international titles: 23, among them a record 16 Copa Américas.
Argentina.evidence: Argentina has won the Copa América a record 16 times, most recently in 2024. ... Argentina holds the record for most official international titles, with 23.

Italy.text: Winning in 1934 and 1938, it was the first team to defend the World Cup title.
Italy.evidence: It has won the FIFA World Cup four times (1934, 1938, 1982, and 2006), becoming the first team to successfully defend the title

France.text: Just Fontaine scored 13 goals for France at the 1958 World Cup, a record that still stands.
France.evidence: At the 1958 World Cup, France reached the semi-finals where they lost to Brazil. In the 3rd-place match, France defeated West Germany 6–3 with Fontaine recording four goals, which brought his goal tally in the competition to 13, a World Cup record that still stands today.

England.text: The only World Cup winner never to win its own continent's title, and the only one that isn't a sovereign state.
England.evidence: England are the only team to have won the World Cup at senior level but not their own major continental title, and the only team representing a non–sovereign state to have won the World Cup.

Spain.text: Winning in 2026 made it the first country to hold the men's and women's World Cups at once.
Spain.evidence: Following their 2026 World Cup victory, Spain became the first national team to hold the men's and women's World Cup titles simultaneously and the first national team to win multiple World Cup titles in the 21st century.

Netherlands.text: Its 2006 game with Portugal, the Battle of Nuremberg, set a World Cup record of four red cards.
Netherlands.evidence: They were eliminated in the second round after losing 1–0 to Portugal. The match produced 16 yellow cards, matching the World Cup record for most cautions in one game set in 2002, and set a new World Cup record of four red cards, two per side; it was nicknamed "the Battle of Nuremberg" by the press.

Uruguay.text: Its 1950 final win over Brazil drew 173,850 people, still the record for an official football match.
Uruguay.evidence: Uruguay's fourth title came in 1950 after beating hosts Brazil in the final match 2–1, a match that still holds the record for the highest official attendance for a football match ever (173,850 people at the gate).

Belgium.text: The only team to top the FIFA ranking without ever winning a World Cup or a continental trophy.
Belgium.evidence: To date, Belgium is the only national team to top the FIFA ranking without having won a World Cup or continental trophy.
